column1: # Mega ROADMAP sub-goal line: the one declaration of the box and id grammar (same shape as lib/board/states.tsv).
# A sub-goal line is `- <box> <id> ...`, for example `- [ ] SG-03 Title , auto , depends SG-02` or `- [x] 03-slug (repo), prose, PR #9`.
# Every reader derives from this file: bash through lib/mega/box.sh, Python through lib/mega/box.py.
# tests/test-mega-box.sh fails when a reader hardcodes the grammar again.
# Columns are TAB-separated: kind, name, token, class, aliases.
#   kind box  a checkbox. `token` is the canonical form a writer stamps; `aliases` are legacy forms every reader also accepts
#             (space-separated, `-` for none). Stored ROADMAPs keep their alias forms; a writer only ever writes the token.
#   kind id   a sub-goal id as an ERE. A reader that accepts "any sub-goal" ORs every id row; a reader tied to one id form
#             (the orchestrator drives SG-NN only: its goal file, branch and `depends` tokens are SG-based) names the row.
#   class     active    open work a runner may pick up
#             hold      parked on purpose: counts as not done, is never auto-picked, never makes a mega "active"
#             terminal  done
#   id rows carry `-` for class and aliases.
# A box token is exactly `[` + one character + `]`; the character must not be one of `] ^ \`.
# Order matters: it is the order of `box.sh machine`.
box
box
box
id
